citation: Cat Tweedie session, Clean up log, 2026-07-15
name: I get to be cared for
summary: Settle, recall being held or cared for, notice what the nervous system does when you do, then name out loud what it would actually take to feel well taken care of — money, friends, health, successors, collaborators — instead of what you can tolerate alone. Reach for it on a keyed-up morning when the tone underneath the check-in is 'the good life requires my herculean effort' or 'I have to push myself,' before the taskmaster has picked its target for the day. This is the resourcing sit; it goes first, and everything harder goes after it.

steps.title: 1. Settle
steps.text: Sit and let the belly out. Three or four long exhales, longer than the inhales. Don't work on anything yet — just let the body notice it has stopped moving.

steps.title: 2. Being cared for
steps.text: Bring up one time you were cared for. Someone who fed you, drove you, sat with you, stayed. Get the specifics: where you were, what their voice sounded like. Then say to yourself, slowly: 'I get to be cared for.'

steps.title: 3. What would it take?
steps.text: Ask: 'what would it take for me to feel well taken care of?' Money, friends, health, successors, collaborators. Name them one at a time and be specific and greedy — a teammate who takes these two things off my plate, someone queued up in three years. This question replaces 'what can I do myself or tolerate?', so notice each time you quietly swap it back.

steps.title: 4. Rest in what changed
steps.text: Stop asking. Something in the tone has probably dropped a notch. Sit in that, without trying to hold it or improve it. If the keyed-up tone comes back, that's fine — notice it and return to being someone who gets to be cared for.

steps.title: 5. Close
steps.text: One more long exhale. You are not going to solve the support problem this morning. You only have to leave the cushion still holding the question in its new form.

citation: Cat Tweedie session, Clean up log, 2026-05-26
name: Meet it from resource
summary: The practice Cat named: build resource first, then turn toward the hard thing — rage, terror, shame — metabolize it in your own system through sensation, breath and sound, integrate, and only then move. Reach for it when there is one specific hard feeling waiting and there is enough ground under you to meet it; if the morning is already collapsed or keyed-up, sit the resourcing one first. The whole point is that you go toward it without leaving yourself: 'no need to ever abandon myself.'

steps.title: 1. Resource first
steps.text: Before you name anything difficult, get resourced. Feel the floor, the sit bones, the weight of your hands. Find one place in the body that is genuinely okay right now and stay there until it is obvious. Don't skip this step to get to the interesting part — the order is the practice.

steps.title: 2. Turn toward it
steps.text: Now bring up the challenge. Rage, terror, shame — whichever one is actually here. Let it come close enough to feel in the body, and keep one hand on the resourced place. You are not trying to understand it or decide anything about it yet.

steps.title: 3. Metabolize
steps.text: Metabolize it in your own system. Sensation first: where is it, what shape, is it moving. Then breath into it. Then sound, if sound wants to come — a hum, a groan, an open 'ahhh.' Let it change as many times as it changes. Come back to the resourced place whenever you need to and then go back in.

steps.title: 4. Integrate
steps.text: Stop working it. Let whatever moved settle back into the rest of you. Feel the whole body again, not just the hot part. This is the step the pattern wants to skip, because there is nothing to do in it.

steps.title: 5. Move from coherence
steps.text: From here, notice what you want to do today — not the list, the movement. 'Move from coherence' creates coherence in the world, and there is abundant energy in it, no depletion from service and no recovery needed. This is trust built over time. No need to ever abandon myself.

name: What do I want?
summary: The three diagnostic questions from the rigid and compensated-merging guides, asked one at a time with a long wait for a body answer instead of a head answer. Reach for it when you are stuck in front of a specific commitment or task — decision paralysis, avoidance, the fear of doing the wrong thing, or a yes you suspect the Giver said for you. The blank that comes back is not a failure of the sit; a blank or an 'I should' is the diagnostic that you are in pattern.

steps.title: 1. Pick one thing
steps.text: Settle, and bring one specific thing to mind: a task, a commitment, an invitation, the thing you keep not doing. One thing, concrete, with a person and a deadline attached if it has them. Hold it lightly in front of you.

steps.title: 2. Want, or scared?
steps.text: Ask: 'Am I doing this because I want to, or because I'm scared of what I'll feel if I don't?' Wait. If it is the second, that is the Giver compensation running, not love. You are not deciding anything yet — just reading the instrument.

steps.title: 3. What do I want?
steps.text: Now the big one: 'What do I want?' Ask it and then stop asking, and wait for an answer from the body rather than the head. Tolerate the blank. If what comes back is blank or 'I should,' you are in pattern — note it without correcting it, and ask again. Keep asking for the rest of this step.

steps.title: 4. Thanked and waved off
steps.text: Imagine they thanked you warmly and said you don't need to do that for me. Watch the first thing that moves in your chest. 'Relieved or rejected?' Relief means it was compensation. Don't argue with the answer.

steps.title: 5. The version you fully want
steps.text: Last question: 'what is the version of this that I fully want?' Not the tolerable version, not the responsible version. Let the body sketch it, even if it seems impractical. Then get up and go find out.

citation: Jeff Lieberman call, Clean up log, 2026-07-09
name: Where's the suffering?
summary: Ask where the suffering actually is, find that the answer is the nervous-system tone rather than any of the problems, and have compassion for the tone itself — then witness the controlling as it arises, since you can't force yourself to stop controlling. Reach for it on an anxious, planning, gripping morning: the check-in is full of contingencies, the mind is already three moves ahead, and every item feels like it needs managing. If crying comes, let it — 'it's not a crying to make things stop. It's a shedding.'

steps.title: 1. Settle
steps.text: Sit. Let the planning keep running for a moment; don't fight it. Just add the body underneath it — floor, sit bones, breath — so there is something else in the room besides the thinking.

steps.title: 2. Where's the suffering?
steps.text: Ask: 'Where's the suffering?' Not which problem is worst — where, in you, right now. The answer is the nervous system tone. Find it: the hum, the grip, the leaning-forward quality. Now have compassion for that, the way you would for a person who has been holding that tone for years.

steps.title: 3. You can't force yourself to stop
steps.text: Notice the impulse to fix the tone. That is more control. 'You can't force yourself to stop controlling — that's just more control.' Let the impulse be there and don't act on it, and don't make not-acting into another project.

steps.title: 4. Witness how it arises
steps.text: The only way through is witnessing. So watch: how does the controlling arise? As thoughts? As sensations? Where does it start, what comes first, how long does one round last? All of it is witnessable, and all control mechanisms are just content. Stay with the arising for the rest of this step, without concluding anything.

steps.title: 5. Shedding
steps.text: If something wants to come up — tears, a shake, a long exhale — let it. 'It's not a crying to make things stop. It's a shedding.' Nothing has to be different by the end of this sit.

name: Stay in the collapse
summary: Sit in the crash instead of climbing out of it: don't rebuild the Giver, don't find someone new to help, and use the shame question to get underneath it — 'what would I have to feel if I couldn't feel ashamed right now?' Reach for it in collapse mode, the sudden drop into depression and self-loathing that lands after a stretch of high competence, when 'I'm weak, I'm a fake, I'm the loser' is running and nothing in the situation explains the size of it. The crash is the system surfacing the real need; rebuilding the compensation buries it again.

steps.title: 1. Arrive in it
steps.text: Sit down in the state you are actually in. Don't posture it into a better one. Slumped is fine. Notice the flavor: heavy, drained, disgusted, done. Name it once and stop talking.

steps.title: 2. Don't rebuild the Giver
steps.text: Watch for the climb-out move: a person to help, a project to take on, a plan for how to not be like this. That is the compensation rebuilding, and it is the loop. Decline it for the length of this sit. Instead let yourself be the one who needs something, and think of one specific person you could ask, and what you would ask for.

steps.title: 3. Underneath the shame
steps.text: Ask: 'What would I have to feel if I couldn't feel ashamed right now?' Wait for it. Grief, fear, anger, plain hurt — whatever is under the shame's floor.

steps.title: 4. Feel it all the way
steps.text: Now allow that all the way, without defending against it. Shame erodes when you stop defending against it. Stay in the collapse for the rest of this step: no fixing, no lesson, no plan for tomorrow. Ask for help in your head if that is what is here. Receive without repaying.

steps.title: 5. Follow it home
steps.text: Shame is a sign you abandoned part of yourself, and you can follow the shame back to that part. Find whoever it is — probably young, probably the one who was told they hadn't done enough — and stay with them a moment before you get up. Don't make them useful.

name: Radiance of the self
summary: When the self comes up defended and indignant, stay in the intensity of selfing rather than jumping to compassion for the other person, know that the self is radiant, and honor it by staying — then meet its hurt with self-compassion before choosing any response. The same move works on an urge: appreciate the radiance of the urge and of the aversion to it together, and they get released together. Reach for it on a triggered, wronged, or gripped morning — an outrageous accusation still ringing, or a compulsion you have been white-knuckling.

steps.title: 1. Let the self come up
steps.text: Bring up the trigger — what was said, what was done, what you keep reaching for. Let the self come up defended and indignant. This is unjust. Don't talk yourself down and don't reframe it. Let the intensity be as big as it is.

steps.title: 2. Not yet their hurt
steps.text: Notice the fast move to compassion for the other person's hurt. That is the mistaken radiance — it looks generous and it ignores your own. Set it down for now. You will come back to them.

steps.title: 3. Stay in the intensity of selfing
steps.text: Stay in the intensity of selfing and know that the self is radiant. You honor it by staying in the intensity of its response, not by resolving it. Feel where the selfing lives in the body and keep company with it for the rest of this step, and respond to it and its intense experience with self-compassion.

steps.title: 4. Both at once
steps.text: If there is an urge here — the phone, the app, the thing you check — notice the urge and the aversion to the urge as two separate radiances. Appreciate both together. They get released together, or not at all.

steps.title: 5. Respond
steps.text: Now, with your own intensity fully honored, let the other person's hurt back in. Choose how you want to respond while honoring the intensity and hurt on both sides. You may find you don't need to respond today at all.

name: A lot of care to give
summary: Sit with two questions — 'What would it feel like to be love?' and 'What would it feel like to have a lot of care to give?' — and with the thing that makes them feel draining: you conflate care with the display of care, and performing care is exhausting. Reach for it before a hard conversation with Jamie, before a date, or on any morning where the relational fear is that you will not be able to control yourself and will be rejected for it. Nothing has to be decided here; belief updates occur naturally when you give your emotions a safe environment.

steps.title: 1. Name the person
steps.text: Settle, and bring one person to mind — the conversation you are walking into, the date, the friend you have been avoiding. Just their face. Notice what the body does when they arrive.

steps.title: 2. What would it feel like to be love?
steps.text: Ask: 'What would it feel like to be love?' Not to act loving. To be it. Let the body try the posture on and report back. Wait for sensation rather than an answer.

steps.title: 3. Care is not the display of care
steps.text: Now: 'What would it feel like to have a lot of care to give?' If that lands as draining, that is the conflation — you are hearing it as a display of care you would have to perform, and performing care is exhausting. Separate them. The care is the thing under the skin; the display is a decision you can make later, or not.

steps.title: 4. Omnidirectional
steps.text: The fear is that if you had a lot of care you wouldn't be able to control it and would be rejected. The wisdom is that care is omnidirectional and includes your selves. So aim some of it inward and let it keep going in every direction at once, with no recipient and no display, for the rest of this step.

steps.title: 5. A safe environment
steps.text: Don't try to conclude anything about the relationship. Belief updates occur naturally when you give your emotions a safe environment — they are perfectly calibrated to your past, not to your present. Be the safe environment for a minute, and then go.

name: Unearned pleasure
summary: Pleasure defined the plain way — awareness of sensations in the body without resistance — practiced on purpose with nothing earned and nothing produced, including the part where the rigid voice calls it lazy. Reach for it after a stretch of pushing, on the morning after a big shipping week, or any time rest feels forbidden and the only legible reason to sit is that it makes you more effective. As you learn to accept sensation, pleasure grows and doesn't really end; the voice calling this lazy is the voice you are trying to disidentify from.

steps.title: 1. Nothing to earn
steps.text: Sit without a goal for the sit. You are not calming down for the meeting, not building concentration, not processing anything. Let the body find the position it actually wants, even if it is a slouch.

steps.title: 2. One sensation, no label
steps.text: Find one raw sensation. Warm air on the back of a hand, weight in the hips, the taste in your mouth. Don't rate it, don't decide whether it is pleasant. Just feel it, and let attention stay longer than it wants to.

steps.title: 3. Drop the resistance
steps.text: Pleasure is awareness of sensations in your body without resistance. So go looking for the resistance instead of the pleasure — the small bracing, the slight lean away, the monitoring. Each time you find one, let it go and see what is underneath. Let attention widen across the whole body for the rest of this step, and take pleasure in whatever it finds.

steps.title: 4. The voice that calls it lazy
steps.text: Somewhere in here the rigid voice will say this is lazy, or that you should be doing something. Hear it and name it as not you. That is the voice you are trying to disidentify from. Then go back to the sensation without arguing with it.

steps.title: 5. Safe enough to enjoy being alive
steps.text: If we are safe, then naturally we take pleasure in being alive. Check whether that is true right now, in this room, on this floor. Then let the last minute be as enjoyable as it is willing to be.

citation: Cat Tweedie session, Clean up log, 2026-07-15
name: Grief of unfulfilled visions
summary: Grieve the futures that didn't happen, hold them less tightly, and practice envisioning the feelings you wanted rather than the formats you imagined them arriving in — then turn to gratitude for the skills the old visions built in you. Reach for it on a disillusioned, dispirited morning, when you are comparing yourself to the missionary version of you from four years ago and doubting you will do the work you now know you need to do. There's no such thing as failure, only learning; and grief shared is not a burden on friends but an opportunity for intimacy.

steps.title: 1. Let the visions come
steps.text: Settle, and let the fantasy machinery run for a minute the way it does in the shower. The perfect future lives. Let the specific ones show up — the community, the house, the version of you who was sure. Notice the grief that comes with each one.

steps.title: 2. Hold them less tightly
steps.text: You are not giving them up. You are loosening your grip. Find where in the body the holding actually is — jaw, chest, hands — and let the pressure off a little. Watch whether the vision survives being held loosely.

steps.title: 3. The feeling, not the format
steps.text: Now drop the format. Not co-housing, not the ten-to-twenty-year community, not any particular instantiation. Underneath each vision is a feeling you wanted to have. Find that feeling directly, in the body, and stay in it for the rest of this step — the feeling is the thing you were actually after, and it has many more doors than the one you had drawn.

steps.title: 4. Gratitude for the skills
steps.text: The missionary phase built a whole way of moving in you. There is no way you could build what you are here to build without having developed it. Feel gratitude for the skills the old vision taught you, even where the vision itself didn't hold. There's no such thing as failure, only learning.

steps.title: 5. Honoring them with intimacy
steps.text: Pick one friend. Notice the reflex that says you would be burdening them with this grief, then try the other frame: 'honoring them with an opportunity for intimacy and a chance to be with me.' Decide whether you will tell them today.

citation: Cat Tweedie session, Clean up log, 2026-07-15
name: A new operating system
summary: Cat's invocation, read slowly in five passages with silence between them: naming the old belief that creating takes Herculean effort and that it isn't safe to rest, then installing the new one — tuning desire, constant dialogue with the body, creation as an extension of caring for yourself. Reach for it when the belief itself is running rather than any particular problem: 'I have to push myself,' 'if I slow down and rest, I'll live a mediocre life,' the keyed-up tone under everything. This one is received rather than worked; the last step is simply resting inside it.

steps.title: 1. The old operating system
steps.text: Read each passage slowly, out loud if you can, and let the rest of the step be silence. — I've been living according to a set of beliefs about what it means to create. I've been believing that it takes incredibly hard work and Herculean effort, and that it's not safe for me to rest and be supported. I am welcoming a recognition of the impact that this has had on my life. I am welcoming a recognition of what it's been like to live in my body with these beliefs at play. I am allowing the many layers of compression stemming from my innocent and beautiful impulse to create my highest potential in the best way that I knew how at the time. There are many layers of compressed emotion in my system from the years of living in this way.

steps.title: 2. The transition point
steps.text: I am in a transition point, and am welcoming a new operating system around how I create. It will feel fundamentally different from this one that I created in my innocence and desire to create a beautiful life for myself. This organizing system that is installing itself in my being is much more comfortable to live inside of. My body gets to be relaxed here. In this operating system, I tune my desire. I feel what I want. I allow myself to feel the joy and pleasure of what I most want to experience. I let that pervade my body.

steps.title: 3. Dialogue with the body
steps.text: In this operating system, I am constantly connected to the joy of getting to create from a place that is an expression of love and care for myself and the people around me. I am in a constant dialogue with the intelligence of my body. My body lets me know when it needs rest. It lets me know when it has new creative ideas and impulses. It lets me know when I want to work out. It lets me know when I want touch. It lets me know the kind of food that I want to eat, and it lets me know when I want time by myself.

steps.title: 4. Rewiring of its own accord
steps.text: By feeling through the full impact of my earlier operating system, and welcoming the discovery of my new one, many aspects of my body, my beliefs, my system begin to rewire of their own accord. They're teaching me that creation is a natural result of existing, and that the way that creation feels will be a match to how I feel about creation. If I assume and feel in my body that I deserve to be cared for, nourished, and supported, then my body will be filled with more joy and inspiration. The places that need attention will naturally present themselves. I don't have to go looking for them. And because I'm taking care of myself with the resource that I deserve in every moment, there is the bandwidth to process what comes up.

steps.title: 5. Surrender, with gratitude
steps.text: There's no separation between taking beautiful care of myself and creating in a way that is beautiful and caring. Creating from a place of harshness and deficit will transmit harshness and deficit into the world. When I create from a place of gentleness, softness, deserving of care, support, abundance — creation will find a way to meet me there. I am willing to learn. I am willing to make the first move inside myself, and welcome the universe to meet me. I am surrendering my old operating system, that was built around avoiding disappointment, with complete honor and gratitude for the intelligence of avoiding disappointment, and the extraordinary operating system that I developed and used and grew inside of for so many years. Thank you.

steps.title: 6. Rest in it
steps.text: Put the words down and rest inside the system they describe. Nothing to install and nothing to repeat. If the old one starts talking, let it — you are honoring it too.

name: I am here
summary: The somatic bottleneck, practiced directly: wiggle your butt, soften your eyes, find one raw sensation, then build toward a felt, embodied 'I am enough, I am here, I have what I need.' Reach for it on a disembodied, in-the-head morning — the check-in is articulate and analytical, you are explaining your state rather than feeling it, or someone recently told you it was hard to feel connected to you. Reading about this doesn't move the needle; feeling does, so this sit deliberately refuses to be interesting.

steps.title: 1. Wiggle butt, soft eyes
steps.text: Before you settle: wiggle your butt on the cushion, move in some way with no correct form and no point to it. Then let the eyes go soft — stop point-focusing, take in the whole scene at once, look at the spaces between things. The mind will say this is pointless. That's the point.

steps.title: 2. One raw sensation
steps.text: Find one sensation and don't put words on it. Pressure of the sit bones. Air temperature on the face. The hands' weight. When the narration starts, notice it and come back to the raw thing. Nothing to conclude.

steps.title: 3. Find the core
steps.text: Now look for the middle of you — the column from the pelvic floor up through the belly and chest. It may be vague or missing; that's the report, not a failure. Breathe there. Feel the belly move. Let the attention live in the trunk rather than the head or the limbs.

steps.title: 4. I am here
steps.text: Say it slowly, inside, and then wait for the body to either confirm it or not: 'I am enough. I am here. I have what I need.' Don't believe it on purpose. Say it, feel what happens, say it again. Spend the rest of this step going back and forth between the sentence and the sensation — this is the bottleneck both patterns end at, and the only way through it is felt.

steps.title: 5. Messy and solid
steps.text: The aspiration is MESSY and SOLID — sovereign, unguarded, expressive, connected to yourself. Not composed. See if you can stand up still in the body rather than back in the head, and carry a little mess with you.

name: If confused, what are the sensations?
summary: The circling learning, run as a sit: when you are confused, go to the sensations; when the sensations oppose each other, see whether you can release grasping rather than resolve them. Reach for it on an ambivalent, torn morning — two true things pulling opposite ways about a person, a group, a commitment — especially when there is shame in the mix about being distracted by your own drama while someone else is sharing something hard. Ends on the pattern line that hit: 'it's not even about love. it's a need to be perfect.'

steps.title: 1. Name the confusion
steps.text: Settle, and name the thing you are torn about in one sentence. Don't argue either side. Notice that the head has been running the same loop on it and hasn't produced an answer.

steps.title: 2. What are the sensations?
steps.text: 'If confused, what are the sensations?' Leave the question and go into the body. Find the two or three that are actually here — throat, chest, gut, hands. Locate them and describe them to yourself in physical terms only: tight, hot, hollow, buzzing.

steps.title: 3. Can you release grasping?
steps.text: If the sensations oppose each other — wanting and dreading, toward and away — don't pick a winner. 'If opposing sensations: can I release grasping.' Feel both at full size at the same time, and each time you notice yourself reaching for a resolution, let that reach go and stay with both. The rest of this step is just that, over and over.

steps.title: 4. The shame about your own drama
steps.text: If there is shame here about being distracted by your own drama while someone else was sharing theirs, let it come up. Feel it in the body rather than explaining it. Notice how quickly the mind wants to work out the correct way to have handled the moment.

steps.title: 5. Not about love
steps.text: Try the line that hit and feel what the body does with it: 'it's not even about love. it's a need to be perfect.' Brutal, and possibly true. Sit with it for a minute and leave without doing anything about it.
